notes:
1. Meaning of Lokpal

  • The Lokpal is a statutory anti-corruption institution functioning at the Union level.
  • It receives and examines allegations of corruption against specified public functionaries.
  • It functions under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.
  • It is an anti-corruption ombudsman rather than a criminal court.
📌 Must-Memorise

Lokpal → Union-Level Anti-Corruption Ombudsman

2. Meaning of the Word Lokpal

“Lok” means:

  • People.

“Pal” means:

  • Protector.
  • Guardian.

Lokpal therefore literally means:

  • Protector of the People.

3. Nature of Lokpal

The Lokpal is a:

  • Statutory Body.
  • Anti-corruption ombudsman.
  • Union-level accountability institution.

It is not a:

  • Constitutional Body.
  • Constitutional Court.
  • General grievance-redress forum.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Lokpal → Statutory Body

Not → Constitutional Body

4. Legal Basis

The Lokpal was established under:

  • Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.
📌 Must-Memorise

Lokpal → Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013

5. First Administrative Reforms Commission

In 1966, the First Administrative Reforms Commission recommended:

  • Lokpal at the Union level.
  • Lokayukta at the State level.
📌 Must-Memorise

1966 → First ARC → Lokpal + Lokayukta

6. First Lokpal Bill

The first Lokpal Bill was introduced in:

  • 1968.
  • Several subsequent legislative attempts failed to become law or lapsed before enactment.
📌 Must-Memorise

First Lokpal Bill → 1968

7. Enactment in 2013

Parliament finally enacted the:

  • Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.
  • This converted a long-standing administrative-reform proposal into a statutory anti-corruption institution.

8. Presidential Assent

The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act received Presidential assent on:

  • 1 January 2014.

9. Commencement

The Act came into force on:

  • 16 January 2014.
📌 Must-Memorise

2013 → Act Passed

1 January 2014 → Presidential Assent

16 January 2014 → Came into Force

10. Need for Lokpal

The institution was intended to provide an independent mechanism for examining credible corruption allegations involving specified Union public functionaries.

It complements existing:

  • Vigilance bodies.
  • Investigative agencies.
  • Departmental authorities.
  • Courts.

11. Objectives of Lokpal

Major objectives include:

  • Receiving corruption complaints.
  • Conducting or ordering preliminary inquiry.
  • Directing investigation.
  • Recommending prosecution.
  • Recommending disciplinary action.
  • Improving accountability.
  • Promoting integrity.
  • Strengthening Rule of Law.
  • Protecting public resources.

12. Lokpal Does Not Replace Existing Agencies

The Lokpal complements rather than replaces:

  • Central Vigilance Commission.
  • Central Bureau of Investigation.
  • Departmental vigilance authorities.
  • Courts.
  • Other statutory enforcement agencies.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Lokpal ≠ CBI

Lokpal ≠ CVC

Lokpal ≠ Criminal Court

13. Composition of Lokpal

The Lokpal consists of:

  • One Chairperson.
  • Not more than eight Members.

14. Maximum Strength

Maximum total strength of Lokpal is:

  • Nine.

This consists of:

  • 1 Chairperson.
  • Up to 8 Members.
📌 Must-Memorise

Lokpal Maximum Strength → 9

15. Judicial Members

At least:

  • 50% of the Members

must be:

  • Judicial Members.
📌 Must-Memorise

Lokpal → At Least 50% Judicial Members

16. Inclusive Representation

Not less than 50% of the Members must belong to categories including:

  • Scheduled Castes.
  • Scheduled Tribes.
  • Other Backward Classes.
  • Minorities.
  • Women.
⚠️ TNPSC Favourite

50% Judicial Members

50% Representation → SC/ST/OBC/Minorities/Women

17. Qualification of Chairperson

According to the source, the Chairperson may be:

  • A former Chief Justice of India.
  • A former Judge of the Supreme Court.
  • An eminent person of impeccable integrity and outstanding ability with at least 25 years of special knowledge and expertise in fields prescribed under the Act.

18. Expertise for Eminent Person

Relevant fields include:

  • Anti-corruption policy.
  • Public administration.
  • Vigilance.
  • Finance.
  • Law.
  • Management.
  • Public affairs.

19. Judicial Member

A Judicial Member may be:

  • Former Judge of the Supreme Court.
  • Former Chief Justice of a High Court.
📌 Must-Memorise

Judicial Member → Former SC Judge / Former HC Chief Justice

20. Non-Judicial Member

A Non-Judicial Member must be a person of:

  • Impeccable integrity.
  • Outstanding ability.

The person must possess at least:

  • 25 years of specialised knowledge and expertise

in one or more fields prescribed by the Act.

21. Appointing Authority

The Chairperson and Members of Lokpal are appointed by:

  • President of India.
📌 Must-Memorise

Lokpal Appointment → President

22. Basis of Appointment

The President makes appointments on the recommendation of:

  • Selection Committee.

23. Selection Committee

The Selection Committee consists of:

  • Prime Minister — Chairperson.
  • Speaker of Lok Sabha.
  • Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha.
  • Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court Judge nominated by CJI.
  • One eminent jurist.

24. Opposition Representation

Where there is no recognised Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, the source states that:

  • Leader of the single largest Opposition party may be included according to the Act.

25. Eminent Jurist

The eminent jurist is nominated by:

  • President

on the recommendation of:

  • First four members of the Selection Committee.

26. Search Committee

The Selection Committee constitutes a:

  • Search Committee.

Its function is to:

  • Identify eligible candidates.
  • Prepare a panel of candidates.

27. Search Committee vs Selection Committee

Search Committee:

  • Assists in identifying candidates.
  • Prepares a panel.

Selection Committee:

  • Makes the recommendation for appointment.

President:

  • Formally appoints Chairperson and Members.

28. Selection Committee Not Bound by Search Panel

  • The Selection Committee is not bound to select only from the panel prepared by the Search Committee.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Search Committee → Prepares Panel

Selection Committee → Recommends

President → Appoints

29. Term of Office

The Chairperson and Members hold office for:

  • Five years.
  • Or until attaining 70 years of age.
  • Whichever is earlier.
📌 Must-Memorise

Lokpal Term → 5 Years or Age 70, Whichever Earlier

30. Reappointment

According to the source:

  • Chairperson and Members are not eligible for reappointment.

31. Removal

For proved misbehaviour:

  • Removal involves an inquiry by the Supreme Court.
  • President acts according to the statutory removal framework.
📌 Must-Memorise

Lokpal Misbehaviour Removal → Supreme Court Inquiry → President

32. Other Statutory Grounds

The source notes that specified statutory grounds may permit removal:

  • Without the same Supreme Court inquiry used for proved misbehaviour.

33. Independence Safeguards

Institutional independence is supported through:

  • Broad-based Selection Committee.
  • Search Committee.
  • Fixed tenure.
  • Inclusive composition.
  • Qualification requirements.
  • Protected removal procedure.
  • Judicial safeguards.

34. Meaning of Jurisdiction

Jurisdiction identifies:

  • Persons covered by Lokpal.
  • Corruption matters that may be examined under the Act.

Powers identify:

  • Actions Lokpal may take once a valid complaint comes before it.

35. Persons within Jurisdiction

The source states that jurisdiction extends to specified categories including:

  • Prime Minister, subject to statutory limitations.
  • Union Ministers.
  • Members of Parliament.
  • Central public officials.
  • Other bodies and persons covered under the Act.

36. Prime Minister

The Prime Minister falls within Lokpal jurisdiction:

  • Subject to special statutory safeguards and exclusions.
⚠️ TNPSC Favourite

Prime Minister → Covered

But → Subject to Statutory Exceptions

37. Prime Minister — Restricted Areas

The source identifies statutory restrictions relating to matters such as:

  • National security.
  • International relations.
  • External affairs.
  • Public order.
  • Atomic energy.
  • Space.

38. Members of Parliament

Members of Parliament may fall within Lokpal's statutory jurisdiction concerning covered corruption allegations.

However:

  • Parliamentary privileges remain constitutionally protected.

39. Article 105 Protection

Parliamentary:

  • Speeches.
  • Votes

protected under Article 105 are outside Lokpal jurisdiction according to the source.

📌 Must-Memorise

Article 105 → Parliamentary Speech/Vote Protection

40. Complaint Scrutiny

When a complaint is received, the Lokpal may first examine:

  • Whether it falls within jurisdiction.
  • Whether sufficient grounds exist for further action.

41. Preliminary Inquiry

A Preliminary Inquiry is:

  • Initial scrutiny.
  • Limited examination.

Its main purpose is to determine:

  • Whether sufficient grounds exist for detailed investigation.

42. Investigation

Investigation is:

  • A detailed criminal evidence-gathering process.

It seeks to determine:

  • Relevant facts.
  • Evidence.
  • Responsibility.

43. Preliminary Inquiry vs Investigation

Preliminary Inquiry:

  • Initial stage.
  • Limited scrutiny.
  • Determines whether investigation is warranted.

Investigation:

  • Detailed stage.
  • Collects criminal evidence.
  • Conducted by an authorised investigating agency.

44. Lokpal's Powers after Complaint

The Lokpal may, according to the statutory framework:

  • Scrutinise complaints.
  • Order preliminary inquiry.
  • Direct investigation.
  • Recommend prosecution.
  • Recommend disciplinary action.

45. Lokpal Does Not Conduct Every Criminal Investigation

The source specifically distinguishes:

  • Lokpal → Inquiry and statutory oversight.
  • Investigative agency → Detailed criminal investigation.

46. Lokpal and CBI

The CBI may conduct investigations connected with Lokpal-referred corruption matters under the statutory framework.

Therefore:

  • Lokpal exercises statutory supervisory/oversight functions.
  • CBI conducts criminal investigation.

47. Lokpal vs CBI

Lokpal:

  • Anti-corruption ombudsman.
  • Receives and scrutinises complaints.
  • May order or supervise investigation.
  • Does not itself conduct criminal trial.

CBI:

  • Investigating agency.
  • Collects evidence.
  • Conducts criminal investigation in matters lawfully entrusted to it.

48. Lokpal and CVC

The Lokpal functions alongside the:

  • Central Vigilance Commission.

The institutional framework requires coordination between:

  • Lokpal.
  • CVC.
  • Departmental vigilance authorities.
  • Investigative agencies.

49. Lokpal vs CVC

Lokpal:

  • Deals with corruption complaints against specified public functionaries.
  • Exercises powers under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act.

CVC:

  • Supervises vigilance administration within its statutory sphere.

The institutions are:

  • Complementary.
  • Not identical.

50. Recommendation for Prosecution

Where the statutory process establishes sufficient grounds, Lokpal may:

  • Recommend or initiate steps toward prosecution according to law.

51. Disciplinary Action

Apart from criminal prosecution, Lokpal may also recommend:

  • Departmental action.
  • Disciplinary proceedings

where appropriate under the statutory framework.

52. Special Court

Criminal trial is conducted by:

  • Special Court.

The Special Court determines:

  • Guilt.
  • Acquittal.
  • Criminal punishment.

53. Lokpal vs Special Court

Lokpal:

  • Inquires into corruption complaints.
  • Statutory accountability authority.
  • Does not convict accused persons.

Special Court:

  • Conducts criminal trial.
  • Determines criminal guilt.
  • Awards punishment where legally established.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Lokpal → Inquiry/Oversight

CBI → Investigation

Special Court → Trial

54. Ombudsman vs Court

Ombudsman Institution:

  • Examines complaints.
  • May conduct inquiry.
  • May initiate or recommend statutory action.

Court:

  • Delivers binding judicial decisions.
  • May convict or acquit.
  • Grants judicial remedies.

55. Lokpal and Article 14

Although Lokpal itself is statutory, its work supports the constitutional principle of:

  • Equality Before Law.
  • Non-arbitrary administration.

Public position alone should not place a person outside lawful accountability.

56. Rule of Law

Lokpal strengthens Rule of Law by promoting:

  • Legal accountability.
  • Fair inquiry.
  • Institutional scrutiny.
  • Action against corruption within statutory limits.

57. Public Accountability

The institution strengthens accountability by creating a specialised mechanism to examine:

  • Corruption complaints involving specified public functionaries.

58. Integrity in Administration

The Lokpal framework promotes:

  • Integrity.
  • Transparency.
  • Responsible public service.
  • Protection of public resources.

59. Importance of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act

The Act is significant because it:

  • Created an independent statutory anti-corruption authority.
  • Brought specified senior public functionaries within an accountability framework.
  • Established preliminary-inquiry and investigation procedures.
  • Connected Lokpal with existing vigilance and investigating agencies.
  • Improved access to an anti-corruption complaint mechanism.

60. Timely Appointments

Effective functioning depends upon:

  • Timely appointment of Chairperson.
  • Timely appointment of Members.
  • Adequate staffing.

61. Investigative Capacity

The effectiveness of Lokpal also depends upon:

  • Availability of competent investigation.
  • Coordination with investigating agencies.
  • Timely evidence collection.

62. Coordination

Effective anti-corruption enforcement requires coordination with:

  • CBI.
  • CVC.
  • Departmental vigilance authorities.
  • Prosecuting authorities.
  • Special Courts.

63. Complaint Scrutiny

The institution requires:

  • Proper scrutiny of complaints.
  • Efficient identification of genuine allegations.
  • Timely disposal.

64. Prosecution Sanction and Delay

The source identifies timely prosecution-related action as important to effective functioning.

Unnecessary delay can weaken:

  • Accountability.
  • Enforcement.
  • Public confidence.

65. Public Awareness

Citizens need awareness regarding:

  • Lokpal's jurisdiction.
  • Complaint mechanism.
  • Difference between Lokpal and other grievance authorities.
  • Limits of Lokpal's powers.

66. Legislation Alone Is Not Enough

The existence of an Act by itself does not guarantee successful corruption control.

Effective implementation requires:

  • Independence.
  • Staff.
  • Investigation.
  • Coordination.
  • Timely decision-making.
  • Public awareness.

67. Must-Know Facts

  • Lokpal → Union-level anti-corruption ombudsman.
  • Lokpal → Statutory Body.
  • Lokpal → Not a Constitutional Body.
  • Lokpal → Not a criminal court.
  • 1966 → First Administrative Reforms Commission.
  • First ARC → Lokpal at Union + Lokayukta in States.
  • First Lokpal Bill → 1968.
  • Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act → 2013.
  • Presidential assent → 1 January 2014.
  • Commencement → 16 January 2014.
  • Composition → 1 Chairperson + up to 8 Members.
  • Maximum strength → 9.
  • Judicial Members → At least 50%.
  • SC/ST/OBC/Minorities/Women → Not less than 50% representation among Members.
  • Chairperson → Former CJI / former SC Judge / qualified eminent person under Act.
  • Judicial Member → Former SC Judge or former HC Chief Justice.
  • Expertise period for specified eminent/non-judicial category → 25 years.
  • Appointment → President.
  • Recommendation → Selection Committee.
  • Selection Committee Chairperson → Prime Minister.
  • Speaker of Lok Sabha → Member of Selection Committee.
  • LoP Lok Sabha → Member.
  • CJI or nominated SC Judge → Member.
  • Eminent jurist → Member.
  • Search Committee → Prepares candidate panel.
  • Selection Committee → Not bound by Search Committee panel.
  • Tenure → 5 years or age 70, whichever earlier.
  • Reappointment → Not permitted according to source.
  • Misbehaviour removal → Supreme Court inquiry.
  • Prime Minister → Covered subject to statutory restrictions.
  • Article 105 → Parliamentary speeches and votes protected.
  • Preliminary Inquiry → Initial scrutiny.
  • Investigation → Detailed evidence gathering.
  • Lokpal → Does not convict.
  • CBI → Investigation.
  • Special Court → Criminal trial.
  • Lokpal + CBI + CVC → Complementary institutions.
  • Lokpal → Supports Rule of Law, accountability and integrity.
